newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki sinks, weaker U.S. unlocks profit - takers.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki sinks, weaker U.S. unlocks profit - takers.

text.p: Shares succumbed to a U.S.-led pre-weekend bout of profit-taking on Friday, with dollar weakness hitting Nokia particularly but the mood calm and much hanging on the U.S. and H1 reports next week, brokers said.
The FOX portfolio index fell 1.74 percent to 1,235, the HEX all-share index two percent to 3,610. Volume was a solid 800 million markka.
The FOX's fall left the index virtually static on the week.
"Some people saw clear signs of a key reversal on the U.S. stock market on Thursday, which could be a signal for the rising trend to end," one broker said.
Nokia ended down 21.00 markka or nearly five percent at 471.00, about where it started this month before its H1 report triggered the most recent spurt in a sustained rally.

"For Nokia there is clearly resistance at 500 but nobody can say what the support level is after the sharp rises," the broker said. Nokia's chart shows a wall of gains, but it only rose through the 400 psychological barrier on July 4.

Forestries struggled after earlier in the week gathering some pace in response to optimistic comments with the first batch of H1 reports. Another broker said sentiment was still mixed on the cycle in the run-up to H1 news from the majors.
Merita, which has ramped up partly on anticipation of solid investment gains ahead of its H1 next week, gave in 0.50 markka to 23.50 but held well above the 20 area cleared recently.
